quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver must be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Air pollution.
Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with passengers while driving.
Only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things in your car, reading, or daydreaming. Keep watching the road, check your mirrors often, and glance at your instruments regularly. These habits keep you safe.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show you are turning.

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the highway.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have a chance.

questions.question: When driving on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: Round signs warn of:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossings ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs tell drivers that a railroad crossing is coming. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: Smoking while driving:

options.text: Does not affect driving ability.
Helps keep drivers alert.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a distraction.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: An instruction permit costs:
questions.explanation: You must be at least 15 years old to get an instruction permit. This permit lets you practice driving with a licensed adult. The cost is $3.50.

questions.question: When you drive faster, your field of vision:

options.text: Gets wider.
Gets narrower.
Makes it easier to see crossing traffic.
Stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, you must be more alert to dangers around you.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: To enter a freeway correctly, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, signal and match the speed of traffic. Always yield to other vehicles when entering a roadway.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Pull beside them and yell.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half a lane.
Pass in the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other car. Give a motorcyclist a full lane width. Even though there may seem to be room, a motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: Which of these affect how alcohol impacts you?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All three.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Eating slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot stop intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is 20 mph.
You are entering a reduced speed zone.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
You are leaving a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are leaving a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. The "End school zone" sign shows where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: When passing a parked car, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver may open the door as you pass.
Speed up.
Brake hard.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver may open the door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, assume the driver may open the door. Use extra caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You may continue through an intersection with a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow appears with a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a circular green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
You should check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign behind other vehicles. The vehicles ahead pass through and there is no other traffic coming. What should you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign or line before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign or line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip the stop just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Is directly behind your vehicle.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.
